standard_prerequisites.name: The function rho
standard_prerequisites.statement: rho(n) is the least divisor of n that is at least the square root of n.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the function whose average is estimated.

standard_prerequisites.name: The Wasserstein-type identity for Lipschitz statistics
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a bounded Lipschitz function of the normalised logarithmic parts, the expectation of the truncated version equals the expectation of the same function of the Dirichlet limit plus an error of order 1/log x.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is applied twice, to a specific Lipschitz function and to the divisors themselves.

standard_prerequisites.name: Partial summation
standard_prerequisites.statement: Sums of the form sum over n up to x of a quantity divided by log n can be converted into Abel sums.
standard_prerequisites.use: It passes from the normalised sum to the unnormalised asymptotic.

core_obligations: Exhibit the 1-Lipschitz function psi as the infimum of the subset-sums of a point of the simplex intersected with the interval from one half to one, and observe that it is 1-Lipschitz (source lines 256-260).

Identify the left-hand side of the Wasserstein-type identity with the normalised divisor sum, using that the logarithm of rho(n) is the smallest subset sum of the logarithmic parts (source lines 260-263).
Apply the identity and then partial summation to obtain the asymptotic with constant c equal to the expectation of psi of the Dirichlet limit (source line 264).

proof_roadmap.step: Construct the test function and check the Lipschitz bound.
Rewrite the divisor sum as a statistic of the normalised logarithmic parts.
Invoke the Wasserstein-type identity and apply partial summation.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the unlabelled corollary at source lines 248-253: there is a constant c in the open interval from one half to one with sum over n up to x of the logarithm of rho(n) equal to c times x log x plus an error of order x. The author gave it no label, so its position in the article is part of its identity. The proof (source lines 255-265) does not estimate the sum directly: it constructs a specific 1-Lipschitz function of a point of the simplex as the infimum of its subset sums above one half, observes that the logarithm of rho(n) is exactly the value of that function on the normalised logarithmic parts of the factorisation, applies the Wasserstein-type identity of the article, and then converts the normalised statement into the unnormalised asymptotic by partial summation. The statement records the asymptotic and none of the test function, the identification or the summation step.
